messages:
sam: Observed a sharp p95 east-west jump during the 19:05-19:20 batching window on rack-5, affecting gpu-node-5a <-> gpu-node-5b. Jobs saw long tail and a few kube restarts due to probes timing out.

priya: Yep, alerts from the dashboard: p95 token latency doubled and retransmit counter on the NIC spiked. Short grafana snippet:
```
net.tcp.retransmits{node=\"gpu-node-5a\"} 742 -> 1980
net.if.tx_errors{iface=eth0,node=\"gpu-node-5b\"} 12 -> 480
```

hao: quick ethtool dump on 5b shows rx_missed and rx_no_buf increases:
```
ethtool -S eth0 | egrep 'rx_missed|rx_no_buf|tx_err'
rx_missed: 312
rx_no_buf: 89
tx_err: 6
```

infra-bot: ALERT(19:12): Link-layer fragmentation warnings detected on flows crossing tor-5 <-> spine-2; inconsistent MSS/MTU hints in control plane logs. Ticket INF-5087 created.

kim: this smells like inter-frame fragmentation/negotiation rather than pure NIC hardware fault. We had tor-5 firmware push last night that adjusted jumbo handling. Could be ECMP hashing + fragmented frames causing LRO/GRO reassembly failures under the batching burst.

sam: any quick mitigation that doesn't require a switch rollback? Customers in prod experiencing degraded latency.

priya: options off the top:
- temporarily force MTU to 1500 on affected nodes (fast, avoids fragmentation but loses jumbo throughput)
- disable LRO/GRO on those interfaces to avoid reassembly stalls (low-risk test)
- apply pod topology constraints so batch pods stay strictly rack-local until we fix the fabric
- rate-limit batch ingress at the scheduler level during the window (cheap but throughput hit)

hao: I ran a micro-test flipping GRO off on gpu-node-5b and pushed a synthetic burst: p95 dropped ~30ms in the test. Command used:
```
ethtool -K eth0 gro off lro off
# simulate burst via perf client
```

kim: good datapoint. But turning GRO/LRO off cluster-wide reduces cpu offload benefits and increases host CPU while handling packets. Prefer targeted node-level change and measure for an hour.

priya: also saw chksum offload toggles flip in logs on tor-5 after the firmware update. If checksum offload behavior changed, it could confuse the host NIC driver's coalescing heuristics.

sam: can we combine mitigations: annotate nodes to avoid new batch placements + disable GRO on affected nodes for immediate relief? That keeps throughput for other racks intact.

ops-bot: NOTE: kube annotate command template:
kubectl annotate node gpu-node-5a redwood/no-batch=true && kubectl annotate node gpu-node-5b redwood/no-batch=true
(annotate will be honored by batch-scheduler within ~30s)

hao: I'll prepare a small script to toggle GRO/LRO and capture metrics pre/post. Will push to infra-scripts and run in 10m.

priya: I'll open a short-lived rolling change to set the annotation and add a circuit-breaker in the batch scheduler to reduce max batch size for rack-5 while we validate.

kim: pinging network team now to confirm whether tor-5 was fully rolled or partially applied across ports. If only some ports negotiated jumbo, you can get asymmetric paths that fragment on spine.

infra-bot: oncall-net paged at 19:28. Ticket INF-5087 updated with NIC counters and initial GRO test results.

sam: assign actions:
- hao: toggle GRO/LRO test, post metrics (ETA 15m)
- priya: annotate nodes + reduce batch window for rack-5 (ETA 10m)
- kim: confirm TOR firmware roll details with network team & vendor (ETA 45m)
- ops-bot: draft customer note for impacted tenants in us-west (ETA 25m)

hao: running the GRO toggle now on gpu-node-5b (will keep it scoped, no container restarts).

(5m later)
hao: quick results: p95 for synthetic burst: before 118ms -> after 82ms. CPU on host +1.2% under load. Capturing counters and uploading to INF-5087.

priya: annotations applied, scheduler respecting no-batch on those nodes. New batch placements shunted to rack-4 for now. We'll monitor cost impact and throughput.

kim: network team confirms tor-5 had a mixed-port jumbo enablement due to a partial rollout of the firmware. Vendor says they can push a consistent config during a maintenance window or rollback last nights change.

sam: good. For immediate mitigation we will keep GRO off on the two nodes, keep nodes annotated no-batch, and monitor the next peak window. If the vendor can't apply a consistent jumbo config soon, we'll either set MTU to 1500 cluster-wide for that rack or require strict topology pinning for batch jobs.

ops-bot: FOLLOWUP(20:05): mitigation schedule proposed: 02:30 UTC maintenance to either (A) set tor-5 and spine-2 to consistent jumbo=9000 across all ports, or (B) force node MTU to 1500 on rack-5 nodes if (A) is not possible within SLA. Ops will pick option (A) if vendor confirms.

sam: thanks team. Let's keep messages clipped here and move detailed logs into INF-5087. If anyone sees a reoccurrence before the maintenance, ping this thread and escalate to oncall-net.

priya: noted, will also add a metric alert for asymmetric mtu/fragment events so we get an automated indicator next time.

infra-bot: INCIDENT: status=investigating, incident_id=INF-5087
